slides.title: Site Considerations
slides.teach: These are design tradeoffs. Learn why each factor matters rather than memorizing the words alone.

slides.title: Hot Site
slides.raw:
Hot Site
Fully equipped
Up-to-date infrastructure
Ready-to-move
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: A hot site is a disaster-recovery location that is fully equipped and ready to take over operations quickly, often with current systems and replicated data.
course.why: Fast recovery reduces downtime but costs more because duplicate capacity must be maintained.
course.example: A financial company maintains a second data center with active infrastructure and near-current data so critical services can fail over quickly.

slides.title: Cold Site
slides.raw:
Cold Site
Basic infrastructure
Lacks operational components
Take time to be ready
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: A cold site provides basic facility space, power, and connectivity but little or no ready computing equipment or current data.
course.why: It is inexpensive to maintain but takes the longest to become operational after a disaster.
course.example: A company contracts for an alternate building with power and network access but would need equipment delivered and backups restored.

slides.title: Warm Site
points: Middle ground between hot and cold sites
slides.raw:
Warm Site
Middle ground between hot and cold sites
Partial infrastructure
Faster activation than cold site
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: A warm site has some infrastructure and configuration in place but requires additional setup, data restoration, or equipment before full operation.
course.why: It balances recovery speed and cost between hot and cold sites.
course.example: A recovery facility has servers and network connectivity but requires current backups to be restored before applications can run.
course.exam: Warm = partially ready, middle cost and recovery time.

slides.title: Geographic Dispersion
slides.raw:
Geographic Dispersion
Multiple geographic location
Risk mitigation
Complexity
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: Geographic dispersion places redundant resources far enough apart that one local or regional event is unlikely to affect all of them.
course.why: Redundancy inside one building does not help if the entire building loses power or is destroyed.
course.example: Production runs in two cloud regions hundreds of miles apart rather than two racks in the same data center.
